labels.description: Adds a new bullet listing uncertain global trade policies and related government actions, including tariffs, as an adverse economic trend that could hurt consumer and business spending and stakeholder relationships.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new risk (trade policy and tariff uncertainty) is disclosed; the page footer changes are ignorable.

labels.description: Share of revenue generated from activities outside the U.S. rises from approximately 70% (2024) to approximately 71% (2025).
labels.rationale: criterion 4: a share-of-revenue figure changes (70% to 71%) beyond the routine year roll-forward.

labels.description: Adds a sentence that Mastercard or its customers could take, or be perceived to take, actions related to high-risk merchant industries (adult content, firearms, alcohol, tobacco) that could be viewed negatively and result in threats or other retaliatory actions.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new exposure (threats and retaliation over actions toward these industries) is disclosed.

labels.description: ESG disclosures, statements and metrics are now at risk of being viewed as "inaccurate or unlawful" rather than only "inaccurate", and the DEI initiative language is softened ("participate equitably" and "equal opportunities for all of our employees" become "participate" and "where everyone has the opportunity to succeed").
labels.rationale: criterion 3: scope widened by adding the possibility that the company's own ESG statements are viewed as unlawful, a new legal exposure (also criterion 1); the initiative rewording alone would be stylistic.

labels.description: Removes the disclosure that employees may have different career motivations such as project-based or gig work, drops "our ability to innovate" from the listed consequences, and narrows the competitive skill-set market from "technology and other areas important to growth" to "emerging technologies".
labels.rationale: criterion 1: previously disclosed exposures (gig/project-based career motivations and harm to ability to innovate) are removed, and criterion 3: scope of the talent-competition risk is narrowed.

labels.description: Inherited litigation risk from acquisitions is no longer described as possibly impairing "our ability to successfully finance that business"; it now only increases post-acquisition costs of operations.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a previously disclosed consequence of inherited litigation (financing impairment) is removed, narrowing scope under criterion 3; the page footer deletion is ignorable.

labels.description: Adds that Brazil recently enacted regulation requiring PSOs in Brazil (including Mastercard and Visa) to extend their responsibility for the financial and settlement integrity of payments to merchants, replacing the hypothetical that jurisdictions could require guarantee extensions, adds financial condition to the impact, and drops the "in the U.S." qualifier on recent bank failures.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: a new specific regulation and jurisdiction (Brazil PSO settlement-integrity rule) is referenced, and criterion 3: the guarantee-extension risk moves from hypothetical to realized.

labels.description: Mastercard Foundation's stake is restated from approximately 9.4% of general voting power as of December 31, 2024 to "greater than 5%" with no as-of date.
labels.rationale: criterion 4: the disclosed ownership percentage changes from a point figure of approximately 9.4% to a threshold of greater than 5%.
